title: 3 US Jobs Reports This Week Could Sway the Fed's Rate Call
summary: Tuesday's US ISM factory data opens a jobs-heavy week into Friday's payrolls, with markets now pricing a majority chance of a September Fed hike.
body_markdown:
The catalyst was the Fed's Jackson Hole symposium, where the central bank characterized recent inflation as concerning and said its predominant focus should be on prices.


The inflation backdrop supports that tone. Per[Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/digital-assets/2026/08/31/cme-fedwatch-provides-a-66-chance-fed-will-hike-rates-in-september/) , PCE inflation ran 3.7% over 12 months and 4.1% over 6 months, both well above the Fed's 2% target. The acceleration in the shorter window is the number keeping the hawkish case alive, and it explains why a hike that looked improbable weeks ago is now the market's base case.


## How a Hike Repricing Moves Rate-Sensitive Equities


A shift toward tighter policy ripples straight through interest-rate-sensitive corners of the equity market. Financials tend to sit at the center of that repricing, since higher rates reshape net interest margins and lending conditions, putting names like[JPMorgan Chase (JPM)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/jpm/) and[Goldman Sachs (GS)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/gs/) in focus for investors reading the rate tea leaves.


Industrial bellwethers are equally exposed, because rate expectations feed into capital-investment sentiment and cyclical demand, which is why a company like[Caterpillar (CAT)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/cat/) often trades as a proxy for the market's read on growth and financing costs.


## The Week's Data Arc Into Friday's Payrolls


Tuesday's factory print is only the opening act. The US data calendar then runs through JOLTS job openings, the ADP private-payrolls report, and ISM Services, culminating in Friday, September 4's August Nonfarm Payrolls, the labor reads that carry the most weight in the Fed's calculus. The labor market has shown signs of cooling in recent months, and a softer set of employment figures could complicate the hawkish narrative even as inflation stays elevated.


## What the Data Week Means for US Equities


That is the crux of the week ahead. A resilient jobs picture paired with sticky prices would harden the case for a hike, while clearer labor-market weakness would revive the argument for patience. With the manufacturing data setting the tone Tuesday and payrolls closing the week Friday, investors face a stretch where each release can swing the odds on a decision that will define the near-term path for US equities.
